summary: The September 18 checkpoint completes Strict Mode cleanup within the retained private TablePlugin host binder. It removes controller replacement/disposal machinery and uses ordinary empty-selection cleanup. Two attempts to delete the model/command selection bridge failed imperative selection cases and were rejected. The plan reports 37 Table React cases, 3 copied-UI cases, 4 Chromium cases and an actual Chrome drag; topology, resize and unrelated paste policy are unchanged.

evidence.claim: Dated September 18 execution checkpoint and scoped test/browser results, including rejected deletion experiments.
Original hashes for TablePlugin, private host binding and its contract test match their observed files during recovery; this is only a subset of the required runtime/fixture/runner inputs.

proof.limits: Recovery, not replay. Three retained source hashes match, but a complete original source/fixture/runner/result binding is not recovered. Reported test and Chrome results remain historical claims; no fresh browser or scale acceptance.
